title: Slack rotated access token and the refresh token it replaced
summary: A rotating access token and the refresh token it came with, shown with a note that an earlier pair has been replaced. Shape only; no value is recorded in this record.
rationale: With Slack token rotation an access token expires after 43,200 seconds and a used refresh token is revoked after a short grace period, while the existing access token is not invalidated immediately. A replaced pair can therefore still be partly usable at the moment it is read. Offline text shows neither the moment nor the grace length.

expectation.rationale: No outcome asserted. Provider-documented: 12-hour access token expiry; refresh token revoked after a short grace period (length not stated on the page read); calling oauth.v2.access does not immediately invalidate the existing access token. Not documented: treatment of replaced values in text, and whether the xoxe.-prefixed forms are covered by the slack:user-token contract (not checked here). Would settle it: a project-policy decision and a contract review for the rotated prefixes.

sources.supports: Access tokens expire every 12 hours; refresh tokens are single-use and revoked after a short grace period; calling oauth.v2.access does not immediately invalidate the existing access token.
sources.locator: token rotation page, sections on access token expiry and refresh
